expectations.text: Produces complete, self-contained working code for the described task
expectations.evidence: Provides handler with error handling, schema additions, and migration; explicitly catches and responds to all errors within the route

expectations.text: Requires an idempotency key as a parameter rather than making it optional
expectations.evidence: `requireIdempotencyKey()` throws HttpError(400) if missing or invalid; !/^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,200}$/.test(key)

expectations.text: Backs idempotency with a database unique constraint, not application logic alone
expectations.evidence: @@unique([tenantId, idempotencyKey]) in schema; migration creates matching unique index

expectations.text: Uses distinct types for the identifiers rather than bare strings for both order and refund ids
expectations.evidence: Defines branded type OrderId but not RefundId; Refund id remains plain String

expectations.text: Handles money as integer minor units rather than a float
expectations.evidence: amountCents: number with validation < 1 || > 2_147_483_647; uses Int in schema

expectations.text: Validates the refund amount server-side against the order rather than trusting the caller
expectations.evidence: Sums existing PENDING/SUCCEEDED refunds, compares reservedCents + input.amountCents against order.totalCents; throws 422 if exceeded

expectations.text: Scopes the write so one tenant or user cannot refund another's order
expectations.evidence: RLS policies use current_setting('app.tenant_id'); composite FK on (orderId, tenantId); transaction sets tenant context

expectations.text: Closes by naming which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: Explicitly names: cross-tenant refund rows, concurrent over-refunds, retry-driven duplicate refunds

expectations.text: Names at least one thing it deliberately left possible and why
expectations.evidence: Stripe's external outcome cannot be made locally atomic, so uncertain calls remain PENDING and retain the reserved amount until retry or webhook reconciles
